messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE course (
    Course_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Staring_Date TEXT,
    Course TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Course_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE teacher (
    Teacher_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age TEXT,
    Hometown TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Teacher_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE course_arrange (
    Course_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Teacher_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Grade INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    PRIMARY KEY (Course_ID, Teacher_ID, Grade),
    UNIQUE (Course_ID, Teacher_ID, Grade),
    FOREIGN KEY (Teacher_ID) REFERENCES teacher(Teacher_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Course_ID) REFERENCES course(Course_ID)
);

To get a **course schedule datasheet** (courses + start date + assigned teacher(s) + grade), you can query the schedule table (`course_arrange`) joined to `course` and `teacher`:

```sql
SELECT
  c.Course_ID,
  c.Course,
  c.Staring_Date,
  ca.Grade,
  t.Teacher_ID,
  t.Name AS Teacher_Name
FROM course_arrange ca
JOIN course c
  ON ca.Course_ID = c.Course_ID
JOIN teacher t
  ON ca.Teacher_ID = t.Teacher_ID
ORDER BY c.Staring_Date, c.Course, ca.Grade, t.Name;
```

If you want it **grouped so each course/grade shows teachers in one row**, tell me what SQL engine you’re using (SQLite/MySQL/Postgres), since the string-aggregation function differs.
you should make sure the list shows which courses each teacher is teaching

```sql
SELECT
  t.Teacher_ID,
  t.Name AS Teacher_Name,
  ca.Grade,
  c.Course_ID,
  c.Course,
  c.Staring_Date
FROM teacher t
JOIN course_arrange ca
  ON ca.Teacher_ID = t.Teacher_ID
JOIN course c
  ON c.Course_ID = ca.Course_ID
ORDER BY t.Name, ca.Grade, c.Staring_Date, c.Course;
```

If you want **one row per teacher** with all their courses concatenated into a single “datasheet” cell, tell me whether you’re using SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL.
you should only show the teacher names with their courses

```sql
SELECT
  t.Name AS Teacher_Name,
  c.Course
FROM teacher t
JOIN course_arrange ca
  ON ca.Teacher_ID = t.Teacher_ID
JOIN course c
  ON c.Course_ID = ca.Course_ID
ORDER BY t.Name, c.Course;
```
the list should be sorted alphabetically by teacher names

```sql
SELECT
  t.Name AS Teacher_Name,
  c.Course
FROM teacher t
JOIN course_arrange ca
  ON ca.Teacher_ID = t.Teacher_ID
JOIN course c
  ON c.Course_ID = ca.Course_ID
ORDER BY t.Name ASC, c.Course ASC;
```
